title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.
